messages:
Priya: heads-up: saw a micro-gap in reads during a simulated shard transfer. new owner prefetch finished, old node later applied a hard-evict and cleared residency. new owner served for ~150ms then hit not-resident path -> small spike in latency. anyone familiar?
Max: yup. reproducible. sequence: demote -> new prefetch -> old hard-evict -> prefetch-produced residency is effectively stale. there's no fencing so the stale residency slips through until background validation runs
Jules: sounds like we need a cheap guard on prefetch completion. two ideas: (1) streaming prefetch carries a session id/lease_epoch and completion validates with a single prefix metadata read, or (2) hard-evict writes a tombstone gen that readers check. (1) is lower comp cost; (2) is more robust for eventual consistency
Ketan: agree. (1) seems quickest: attach prefetch.session = lease_epoch|nonce in header, on completion do if prefix.lease != session.lease -> abort. single metadata read. no per-key CASs. add metric for aborted completions
Priya: proposal: implement completion gating (session) first. metric: kv.prefetch.session_abort_count and kv.prefetch.session_abort_pct. alert if pct > 0.5% over 5m. follow-up: opt-in eviction_gen tombstone behind feature flag for canary prefixes
Max: tombstone sketch: hard-evict sets eviction_gen++ and writes tombstone_ts. prefetched batches carry observed eviction_gen; completion compares observed vs current. if current > observed -> abort. read path needs a one-branch check when validating residency. small mem overhead (4 bytes) per prefix but deterministic correctness
Jules: hybrid idea: only write tombstone when handoff path sees demote->hard-evict inside a tight window (e.g., < 60s). avoids extra metadata for normal evicts. good incremental approach
Ketan: plus sticky fallback: if a prefix sees >N aborted completions in T, delay finalizing the handoff by sticky_seconds to reduce oscillation. that helps noisy hot prefixes
Priya: owners: Ketan -> session gating + metrics + traces; Max -> tombstone prototype + perf bench; Jules -> tests + smoke scenarios; Priya -> canary orchestration and rollback runbook
Jules: tests to add: (A) stale session completion should not create residency and increments abort metric; (B) handoff where old writes tombstone and new owner rejects prefetch; (C) canary perf sweep comparing hot-read latency with tombstone enabled vs disabled
Priya: quick canary config snippet for infra:
```
kv.prefetch.session_gate=true
kv.eviction.gen_mode=opt_in  # none|opt_in|always
kv.eviction.opt_in_window_s=60
kv.handoff.sticky_seconds=30
kv.prefetch.abort_alert_pct=0.5
```
Ketan: add trace tags: prefetch.session, prefetch.result, evict.gen_before, evict.gen_after. that'll make console slices easy
Max: perf note: pack eviction_gen into prefix header to avoid extra indirections on read path. single branch check while validating residency should be negligible but I'll quantify on local perf bench
Priya: rollback plan (must be in PR): 1) flip kv.prefetch.session_gate=false 2) kv.eviction.gen_mode=none 3) run tombstone GC job if any tombstones were emitted 4) revert canary images. include commands in PR description
Jules: smoke plan: pick 8 medium-hot prefixes, enable session_gate + opt_in gen_mode for half, run continuous reads for 10m, trigger scripted handoffs every 20s for 5m. assert: no tail spikes >200ms, kv.prefetch.session_abort_pct < 1%, and no duplicate residency metrics
deploy-bot: canary cluster requested with config template. will post when ready
Ketan: one edge-case: long-running prefetch (huge prefix) might hold old observed eviction_gen; ensure completion logic reads current eviction_gen atomically and compares once. avoid per-batch validate to keep overhead low
Max: noted. code sketch: read prefix_meta = load_prefix_meta(prefix_id); if session != prefix_meta.session || prefix_meta.eviction_gen > observed_gen { abort; } else commit residency
Priya: ok. action items: Ketan open PR for session gate + metric + traces; Max open issue for tombstone perf bench and prototype; Jules add tests and harness; I'll wire canary and dashboards. tag me on PRs. closing thread for now, reopen if canary shows anomalies :thumbsup:
